newsitem.title: INDIA: GE Capital plans two-pronged growth in India.
newsitem.headline: GE Capital plans two-pronged growth in India.

text.p: GE Capital, a subsidiary of General Electric Co, said on Tuesday that its strategy for India was to grow both internally and through acquisitions.

The company provided a transcript of an interview that Jeffrey Werner, senior vice-president for Corporate Treasury and global funding operations, gave to the Indian daily Economic Times. He denied that the plan was simply to acquire and grow.
"No...our strategy will be both -- start-up and acquisition, internal growth and acquisition -- wherever appropriate," he said.

"We started in 1993 to build from the ground up each business. If, as a part of this whole environment change...we see there are players that in our target markets, that are well-managed, good asset quality and are well priced and would like to work a friendly deal...we certainly will talk to all of those."
Werner said GE Capital, which established a wholly owned subsidiary in India four years ago and now has 200 employees, was not interested in the financial services business in India.
"Rather, we're interested in being in the automobile financing business, equipment leasing business etc., in India," he said.
